correctness.rationale: For a quadratic restricted to a side segment, the directional derivative at the midpoint equals the difference of endpoint values, so each midpoint-bisection test is exactly one graph-edge equality. For a nondegenerate quadrangle the evaluation map on degree-at-most-two polynomials has kernel equal to the two-dimensional pencil space and is therefore onto \(\mathbb k^4\). Passing a side set means the four evaluations are constant on each connected component; this equals the one-dimensional diagonal exactly for a connected side graph. If the graph is disconnected, the preimage is strictly larger than the net polynomial space, and adding a nonzero pencil polynomial if necessary gives a degree-two counterexample. The entanglement corollary then follows from two opposite-side polynomials spanning the second pencil.

value.rationale: The lead paper highlights side-midpoint bisection as a geometric membership test and specifically notes a reduction from six sides to four. The accepted theorem identifies the exact combinatorial invariant controlling the test in the nondegenerate case, proves the optimal threshold is three, classifies all minimal certificates as the 16 spanning trees of \(K_4\), and reduces an entanglement check to six concrete bisection incidences. This is a natural structural sharpening of the paper's central recognition mechanism, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere recomputation.
